newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds fall on uncertainty over German asset.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds fall on uncertainty over German asset.

text.p: Danish bond prices fell in quiet but cautious trade on Wednesday ahead of Thursday's Constitution Day market holiday with the outlook unsure.

"Ongoing uncertainty about Germany's gold reserves dispute seems to have put a damper on trade even if agreement between Bonn and the Bundesbank seems on the way. Tomorrow's closure here while other markets remain open means that investors are holding back," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.15 point from Tuesday's close at 110.99, yielding 6.32 percent in 1.2 billion crown turnover.

The forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark fell 0.31 point to 103.56 during the morning, about the same as its Tuesday closing level, in 0.6 billion crown turnover, with the yield at 6.50 percent. The 2006 June future rose 0.10 point to 111.00 with 551 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.02 point to 89.20.

The crown traded at an unaltered 3.8082 per mark at 1130 GMT. The 2006's 10-year yield gap with Germany widened two points to 47, the 2007-bund differential was unchanged at 65. The Central Bank was active on the market buying short-term bonds. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom +45-33-969652
